newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop soymeal, soyoil hit contract lows.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop soymeal, soyoil hit contract lows.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures tumbled on Tuesday and contract lows were notched in the new crop months, keying off of weakness in soybeans, pit sources said.
Soyoil also ended lower with contract lows in most months.

Old crop soymeal took a beating, prompted by massive liquidation in July soybeans. The August contract traded as low as $220.20 per ton, or down the expanded $15 limit. That was the lowest level for the August contract since January.
Floor sources said old crop months drew weakness from ideas demand was shifting to new crop but expected bumper crops could easily meet that demand.

USDA on Monday put 1997 soybean plantings at 70.85 million acres, above trade expectation. That forecast, coupled with perceptions of ideal growing weather, led to predictions for a record crop this year.
USDA's weekly crop update released Monday afternoon showed 65 percent of the soybean crop was rated good to excellent, an improvement from 61 percent the previous week.
The new contract low for new crop December is $187.50 per ton. The previous low of $199.00 was set on December 10.
Soymeal ended $13.80 to $8.40 per ton lower with July off $13.80 at $244.20. Soyoil closed down 0.37 t0 0.18 cent a lb.
On the day, commercials were sellers of old crop soymeal, led by Cargill Inc, which sold 400 lots July and 100 August. ADM sold 200 July and Continental Grain sold 200 August.
In soyoil, Prudential Securities and Cargill Investor Services each sold 500 December and Tenco Inc sold 200 December.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 40,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 36,873 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 25,000 lots, against Monday's 34,671 lots.
